findings.element: EX 3 — Consensus Forecast Table, 'Key View' column
findings.detail: The 'Key View' column text is cut off for every institution row (e.g., Goldman Sachs shows 'Tax cuts (One Big Bea…', BCA Research shows 'Two-stage 2026: tech-…'). The column is too narrow to display the full commentary, making the content unreadable at board level.

findings.element: EX 3 — Consensus Forecast Table, 'Range / Scenario' and other columns
findings.detail: Several cells in the Range/Scenario and Key View columns are visibly clipped mid-sentence (e.g., 'fading tariff drag. Al…', 'K-shaped expansion c…', 'gains/month from labor su…'). Content overflow is not handled gracefully.

findings.element: Sector tiles — commentary text beneath each GDP tile
findings.detail: The small-print commentary lines beneath each sector tile (Passenger Airlines, Hotels, Restaurants, etc.) are rendered at an extremely small font size, making them effectively illegible at normal viewing scale for a board deck.

findings.element: EX 4 — Six 2026 themes synthesis block (bottom of page)
findings.detail: The dense paragraph text in the six-theme synthesis section is rendered at a very small size. At board-deck zoom levels this block is unreadable, violating the legibility standard for CEO-facing materials.

findings.element: EX 1 — 'So what' commentary beneath Quarterly GDP chart
findings.detail: The 'So what' note is a single sentence ('The Q4 deceleration into +1.4% is the cleanest run-rate signal — 2026 enters with weaker momentum than the full-year +2.2% suggests.'). Style guide requires a minimum of 2 sentences in per-tab commentary.

findings.element: EX 2 — 'So what' commentary beneath Consensus Indicators chart
findings.detail: The 'So what' note is a single sentence. Style guide requires at least 2 sentences.

findings.element: EX 3 — 'So what' note for Consensus Forecast Table
findings.detail: The 'So what' commentary for EX 3 appears below the table rather than above/preceding it. Per style_guide §1, the fc-note must precede the first chart or table element on the panel.

findings.element: Sector tiles grid — bottom row (Federal Government, Freight & Logistics)
findings.detail: The bottom row of sector tiles contains only two tiles while all other rows contain five, creating a visually unbalanced and incomplete-looking grid layout that may read as missing content to a board audience.

findings.element: EX 1 — Quarterly GDP bar chart
findings.detail: The chart uses two distinct bar colors (green and blue/teal for the Full Year bar) but there is no legend explaining the color distinction between quarterly bars and the full-year aggregate bar.

findings.element: Sector group table — column headers and cell values
findings.detail: The annual GDP contribution table at the bottom of the tab renders column headers (2021–2026F) and numeric cell values at a font size that is extremely small and difficult to read at normal viewing distance, making it unsuitable for a board-level deck.

findings.element: All sector panel commentary lines (e.g., State/Local Govt, Software/Cloud, Freight/Logistics, etc.)
findings.detail: The one- to two-line commentary beneath each sector bar chart is rendered at a very small font size (appears sub-8 pt), making it illegible without zooming in. At board-deck resolution this text cannot be read.

findings.element: Source / footnote line at the very bottom of the dashboard
findings.detail: The full-width footnote string listing data sources (BEA, BLS, FRED, Deloitte, etc.) is rendered in extremely small, low-contrast grey text that is effectively illegible.

findings.element: Sector panel sub-labels — 'GDP Share', '2025 Growth', '2024 Growth', '2023 Growth' toggle bar
findings.detail: The tab-toggle labels and the small 'x% of GDP' sub-labels inside each sector card are rendered at a size that is borderline illegible at board presentation scale.

findings.element: Commercial RE sector panel — commentary text
findings.detail: The commentary text beneath the Commercial RE bar chart appears to be cut off at the bottom of the card, with the final sentence visibly clipped by the panel boundary.

findings.element: GDP Commentary — 'GDP Commentary — 2025 Growth & 2026 Outlook' fc-note block
findings.detail: The commentary block contains more than 4 sentences (it runs to approximately 5–6 distinct clauses/sentences), exceeding the maximum of 4 sentences permitted for fc-note commentary.

findings.element: Bottom sector-contribution table — 'TRENDS' column
findings.detail: The 'TRENDS' column on the far right of the annual GDP table appears misaligned relative to its header; the colored trend badges (Falling/Stable) do not sit flush within the column boundary and appear to overflow or crowd the right edge.

findings.element: Jobs tab
findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.element: Exhibit 5 — Initial Claims line chart axis labels and data labels
findings.detail: The x-axis date labels and the right-axis (continued claims) tick labels in the Initial Claims chart are rendered at a very small font size, making them difficult to read at dashboard viewing scale. Several inline data callout labels along the lines also appear too small to parse without zooming.

findings.element: Bottom footnote / FAQ block (yellow-highlighted Q&A section)
findings.detail: The multi-paragraph FAQ text at the very bottom of the tab is rendered at an extremely small font size (appears to be ~7–8 px equivalent). At board-deck viewing distance this block is completely illegible, defeating its explanatory purpose.

findings.element: Source lines beneath every chart
findings.detail: Source attribution lines are rendered at a font size that is borderline illegible across all charts on the tab. While small source text is conventional, the current size is below the minimum readable threshold for a projected board deck.

findings.element: Exhibit 7 — Industry unemployment table commentary / FAQ block
findings.detail: The 'So what' / FAQ commentary block for the bottom section appears below the industry table rather than preceding the first chart on the tab. Per style_guide §1, the fc-note commentary must precede the first chart it annotates, not follow it.

findings.element: Exhibit 2 — Sector unemployment bar chart (right panel), sector name labels
findings.detail: Several sector name labels on the left axis of the sector bar chart (e.g., 'Information/Tech', 'Leisure & Hospitality', 'Transportation & Warehousing') appear clipped or compressed, with text running very close to the bar area boundary and potentially cut off on the left edge.

findings.element: Exhibit 4 — Annual average unemployment rate line chart, x-axis year labels
findings.detail: The x-axis year labels (1990–2025) are densely packed and several labels appear to overlap or nearly touch each other, reducing readability of the time axis.

findings.element: Exhibit 5 — Initial Claims chart dual-axis series
findings.detail: The chart plots two distinct series (Initial Claims on left axis, Continued Claims on right axis) using different colors and line styles. While a small legend appears to exist at top-right, it is so small as to be nearly invisible, and the dual-axis relationship is not clearly communicated, risking misinterpretation by a board audience.

findings.element: Unemployment Commentary — Trends & Risk Factors (top fc-note)
findings.detail: The commentary block contains more than 4 sentences, exceeding the style_guide §2 limit of 2–4 sentences for per-tab fc-note commentary. The block runs to at least 5–6 distinct sentences.

findings.element: Metric tile — 'Top Sector' KPI card
findings.detail: The sector name 'Investment Banking' is wrapping across three lines and the text appears to overflow or be clipped within the tile boundary, making it visually inconsistent with peer tiles.

findings.element: Exhibit 4 — Sector wage growth horizontal bar chart, Y-axis sector labels
findings.detail: Several sector name labels on the left Y-axis (e.g., 'Hotel Front Desk / Hou...', 'Truck / Freight Drivers', 'T-Commerce (Warehouse)') appear truncated or very tightly packed, making them difficult to read at board-presentation resolution.

findings.element: Exhibit 4 — Sector wage growth bar chart, Y-axis labels
findings.detail: Multiple sector labels are visibly cut off with ellipses (e.g., 'Hotel Front Desk / Hou...', 'Grocery Store (Avg)' area), indicating the label container is too narrow for the full text.

findings.element: Exhibit 3 — Real wages line chart, source/footnote text below chart
findings.detail: The source attribution and methodology footnote beneath Exhibit 3 is rendered at an extremely small font size, well below readable threshold for a board-level presentation.

findings.element: Exhibit 4 — Sector wage growth bar chart, source text below chart
findings.detail: The source line ('SOURCE: BLS CURRENT EMPLOYMENT STATISTICS...') is rendered at a very small size and is barely legible at normal viewing distance.

findings.element: Exhibit 2 — Wage growth line chart, data-vintage/methodology footnote
findings.detail: The multi-line footnote block beneath Exhibit 2 is set in very small type and low contrast, making it effectively illegible in a board deck context.

findings.element: Sector table (Exhibit 5) — 'Trend' column badges
findings.detail: Every single row in the Trend column shows a red 'Falling' badge regardless of the underlying data pattern. If 'Falling' is the semantic 'critical' color, having it applied uniformly to all 18 sectors (including Investment Banking at +5.2% in 2025) suggests either a rendering error or incorrect conditional formatting, which would be called out immediately in a board review.

findings.element: Exhibit 3 — 'So what' callout text
findings.detail: The 'So what —' interpretive sentence appears below the Exhibit 2 chart rather than preceding the first chart on the section, inconsistent with the requirement that fc-note commentary precede the first chart.

findings.element: Gap between Exhibit 2 block and Exhibit 3/4 row
findings.detail: The vertical gap between the Exhibit 2 panel and the Exhibit 3–4 side-by-side row is noticeably larger than the gap between the Exhibit 3–4 row and the Exhibit 5 table below, creating uneven panel rhythm.

findings.element: CPI Commentary panel (Exhibit 1) — body text
findings.detail: The commentary paragraph text is extremely small and low-contrast against the light background, making it effectively unreadable at dashboard viewing size. A CEO-level audience would be unable to read the Fed implications narrative without zooming in.

findings.element: Exhibit 3 — Headline CPI line chart axis labels and annotations
findings.detail: The x-axis date labels, y-axis tick labels, and inline data annotations (e.g., '3.16', 'Fed 2% target') are rendered at a very small font size, making them difficult to read at normal viewing distance in a board deck context.

findings.element: Exhibit 6 — Category-level annual rates table, source footnote
findings.detail: The source footnote below the table is rendered in extremely small type (appears to be ~6–7px equivalent), well below the minimum legible size for a board-level document.

findings.element: Exhibit 5 — Goods vs. services bar chart axis and category labels
findings.detail: Category labels on the y-axis are truncated and very small, making individual category names difficult to distinguish without zooming.

findings.element: Bottom source line (footer across full dashboard)
findings.detail: The full-width source attribution line at the very bottom of the tab is rendered in extremely small, low-contrast gray text that is effectively illegible.

findings.element: Exhibit 5 — horizontal grouped bar chart, y-axis category labels
findings.detail: Several category labels on the left y-axis (e.g., 'Transportation Svcs', 'Medical Care Svcs') appear clipped or abbreviated inconsistently, with text running close to or into the bar area.

findings.element: Exhibit 3 — 'So what' callout box
findings.detail: The 'So what' interpretive commentary for Exhibit 3 appears below the chart rather than preceding it. Per style_guide §1, fc-note commentary must precede the first chart on the panel, not follow it.

findings.element: Exhibit 4 — Energy and transport bar chart 'So what' callout
findings.detail: The 'So what' commentary block for the energy/transport chart is positioned below the chart area rather than above it, violating the rule that commentary precedes the visualization.

findings.element: Exhibit 7 — Trimmed-mean/median CPI line chart, legend and axis labels
findings.detail: The legend entries and x-axis date labels in Exhibit 7 are very small and the legend color swatches are difficult to distinguish at normal viewing size, reducing interpretability for a board audience.

findings.element: Exhibit 4 — Energy and transport horizontal bar chart
findings.detail: The chart panel on the right side of the Exhibit 3/4 row appears to have unequal vertical padding compared to the Exhibit 3 panel on the left, creating a misaligned bottom edge between the two side-by-side panels.

findings.element: Exhibit 4 (Annual CPI bar chart) panel vs. surrounding panels
findings.detail: The vertical gap above Exhibit 4's full-width bar chart panel appears noticeably larger than the gaps between other panels on the tab, creating inconsistent rhythm in the layout.

findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.element: Footer source citations (bottom of page)
findings.detail: The footer text listing all data sources is rendered at an extremely small font size (appears to be ~6-7px), making it completely unreadable at normal viewing scale. Board-level documents require all visible text to be legible.

findings.element: EK 3 Monthly average chart — axis labels and subtitle
findings.detail: The x-axis date labels and the chart subtitle text in the upper-right panel (Section 1, Exhibit 3) are rendered at very small size and appear difficult to read at dashboard viewing distance, particularly the date range annotations along the x-axis.

findings.element: Oil Supply Shock Tracker daily closes chart — x-axis labels
findings.detail: The x-axis date labels on the daily closes line chart (Section 2, EK 5) are extremely small and densely packed, making individual date labels illegible at normal viewing scale.

findings.element: Oil Supply Shock Tracker — x-axis date labels
findings.detail: The x-axis of the daily closes chart (Section 2) shows densely packed date labels that appear to overlap or nearly overlap each other across the ~170 session range, reducing readability.

findings.element: EK 7 Recession signal history chart — x-axis and y-axis labels
findings.detail: The annual WTI chart in Section 4 (EK 7) has very small axis labels and the recession shading annotation text is barely legible at dashboard scale.

findings.element: Full Oil Impact Chain table — body text in route rows
findings.detail: The descriptive body text within each route row of the Impact Chain panel (Section 2, EK 9) is rendered at a very small size, making the supporting detail text difficult to read without zooming in.

findings.element: Section 4 — Recession Signal History commentary block
findings.detail: The orange commentary paragraph in Section 4 contains hedging language ('causality is debated,' 'other factors typically contribute,' 'Worth monitoring') which softens the analytical stance. Style guide prohibits hedging filler in CEO-level commentary.

findings.element: Section 4 — Recession Signal History
findings.detail: The fc-note commentary block in Section 4 appears to sit between the section header and the charts, which is correct in principle, but the block is visually separated from the charts below by significant whitespace, potentially reading as a standalone paragraph rather than a chart precursor.

findings.element: EK 8 — Historical oil price dislocations table, 'Economic Consequence' column
findings.detail: The colored dot annotations and accompanying text in the Economic Consequence column of EK 8 are rendered at a small size that may be difficult to read in a projected board deck environment.

findings.element: Section 3 — Sector Impact table vs. other sections
findings.detail: The Sector Impact section (Section 3) has noticeably more vertical whitespace below the table before the next section header compared to the tighter spacing between Sections 1 and 2, creating inconsistent inter-section rhythm.
